sanskrit: iha vaikasya nāmutra amutraikasya no iha iha cāmutra caikasya nāmutraikasya no iha
english: Here belongs to one person but not the next world; to another the next world but not this one here. Here and the next world to one; to another neither here nor the next world.

sanskrit: dhanāni yeṣāṃ vipulāni santi; nityaṃ ramante suvibhūṣitāṅgāḥ teṣām ayaṃ śatruvaraghna loko; nāsau sadā dehasukhe ratānām
english: Those who possess abundant wealth and always delight in being adorned with fine ornaments — O slayer of the best of foes, this world is theirs; but that higher world is not for those who are ever devoted to bodily pleasure.

sanskrit: ye yogayuktās tapasi prasaktāḥ; svādhyāyaśīlā jarayanti dehān jitendriyā bhūtahite niviṣṭās; teṣām asau nāyam arighna lokaḥ
english: Those who are absorbed in yoga and engaged in austerity, who wear out their bodies in the practice of self-study, who have conquered the senses and are devoted to the welfare of all beings — O slayer of enemies, that higher world is theirs, not this one.

sanskrit: ye dharmam eva prathamaṃ caranti; dharmeṇa labdhvā ca dhanāni kāle dārān avāpya kratubhir yajante; teṣām ayaṃ caiva paraś ca lokaḥ
english: Those who put dharma foremost, who acquire wealth through dharma, and in due time having obtained a wife, perform sacrifices — both this world and the other belong to them.

sanskrit: ye naiva vidyāṃ na tapo na dānaṃ; na cāpi mūḍhāḥ prajane yatante na cādhigacchanti sukhāny abhāgyās; teṣām ayaṃ caiva paraś ca nāsti
english: Those who pursue neither learning, nor austerity, nor charity, who in their delusion make no effort even in procreation, and who, being unfortunate, attain no happiness — neither this world nor the other exists for them.

sanskrit: sarve bhavantas tv ativīryasattvā; divyaujasaḥ saṃhananopapannāḥ lokād amuṣmād avaniṃ prapannāḥ; svadhītavidyāḥ surakāryahetoḥ
english: All of you are possessed of surpassing valour and spirit, endowed with divine energy and excellent bodies; you have descended from that higher world to earth, having studied your learning thoroughly, for the purpose of the gods' work.

sanskrit: kṛtvaiva karmāṇi mahānti śūrās; tapodamācāravihāraśīlāḥ devān ṛṣīn pretagaṇāṃś ca sarvān; saṃtarpayitvā vidhinā pareṇa
english: Having performed great deeds as heroes, practiced austerity, self-restraint, and right conduct, and having duly satisfied the gods, seers, and all the hosts of the departed with proper rites —

sanskrit: svargaṃ paraṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ nivāsaṃ; krameṇa saṃprāpsyatha karmabhiḥ svaiḥ mā bhūd viśaṅkā tava kauravendra; dṛṣṭvātmanaḥ kleśam imaṃ sukhārha
english: — by your own deeds you shall in due course attain the highest heaven, the abode of the righteous. Let there be no anxiety in you, O lord of the Kauravas, upon seeing this present suffering of yourself — you who deserve happiness.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca mārkaṇḍeyaṃ mahātmānam ūcuḥ pāṇḍusutās tadā māhātmyaṃ dvijamukhyānāṃ śrotum icchāma kathyatām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the sons of Pāṇḍu spoke to the great-souled Mārkaṇḍeya: "We wish to hear of the greatness of the foremost brahmins — please tell us of it."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa bhagavān mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ uvāca sumahātejāḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the blessed Mārkaṇḍeya of great austerity, of very great splendour and versed in all scriptures, spoke:

sanskrit: haihayānāṃ kulakaro rājā parapuraṃjayaḥ kumāro rūpasaṃpanno mṛgayām acarad balī
english: A king who established the Haihayas' lineage — a prince endowed with beauty, the conqueror of enemy citadels, mighty — went out hunting.

sanskrit: caramāṇas tu so 'raṇye tṛṇavīrutsamāvṛte kṛṣṇājinottarāsaṅgaṃ dadarśa munim antike sa tena nihato 'raṇye manyamānena vai mṛgam
english: While ranging through the forest overgrown with grass and shrubs, he saw nearby a sage wearing a black antelope skin as an upper garment. That sage was struck down by him in the forest, who mistook him for a deer.

sanskrit: vyathitaḥ karma tat kṛtvā śokopahatacetanaḥ jagāma haihayānāṃ vai sakāśaṃ prathitātmanām
english: Distressed at having done that deed and with his mind struck by grief, he went to the presence of those Haihaya kings of celebrated spirit.

sanskrit: rājñāṃ rājīvanetrosau kumāraḥ pṛthivīpate teṣāṃ ca tad yathāvṛttaṃ kathayām āsa vai tadā
english: That prince with lotus-like eyes, O lord of the earth, then related to those kings exactly what had occurred.

sanskrit: taṃ cāpi hiṃsitaṃ tāta muniṃ mūlaphalāśinam śrutvā dṛṣṭvā ca te tatra babhūvur dīnamānasāḥ
english: Upon hearing of that sage who subsisted on roots and fruits having been killed, and upon seeing it, O dear one, their minds became dejected.

sanskrit: kasyāyam iti te sarve mārgamāṇās tatas tataḥ jagmuś cāriṣṭanemes te tārkṣyasyāśramam añjasā
english: Searching here and there asking "Whose is this man?", all of them went straight to the hermitage of Tarakshya Ariṣṭanemi.

sanskrit: te 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ taṃ muniṃ saṃśitavratam tasthuḥ sarve sa tu munis teṣāṃ pūjām athāharat
english: They all saluted that great-souled sage of firm vow and stood before him; the sage then offered them worship.

sanskrit: te tam ūcur mahātmānaṃ na vayaṃ satkriyāṃ mune tvatto 'rhāḥ karmadoṣeṇa brāhmaṇo hiṃsito hi naḥ
english: They said to that great-souled one: "We are not worthy of your honour, O sage, for a brahmin has been killed through our fault."

sanskrit: tān abravīt sa viprarṣiḥ kathaṃ vo brāhmaṇo hataḥ kva cāsau brūta sahitāḥ paśyadhvaṃ me tapobalam
english: That seer among brahmins said to them: "How was a brahmin killed among you? Where is he? Tell me all together — behold the power of my austerity."

sanskrit: te tu tat sarvam akhilam ākhyāyāsmai yathātatham nāpaśyaṃs tam ṛṣiṃ tatra gatāsuṃ te samāgatāḥ anveṣamāṇāḥ savrīḍāḥ svapnavad gatamānasāḥ
english: Having related all of it to him fully and exactly as it happened, they came together to that place searching — but they did not see the sage there as one departed from life; they were ashamed, their minds wandering as if in a dream.

sanskrit: tān abravīt tatra munis tārkṣyaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ syād ayaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ so 'tha yo yuṣmābhir vināśitaḥ putro hy ayaṃ mama nṛpās tapobalasamanvitaḥ
english: The sage Tarakshya, the conqueror of enemy citadels, spoke to them there: "The brahmin who was destroyed by you — he could be this one; he is my son, O kings, endowed with the power of austerity."

sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭvaiva tam ṛṣiṃ vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ mahad āścaryam iti vai vibruvāṇā mahīpate
english: Upon seeing that sage they were filled with the highest astonishment, exclaiming "This is a great wonder indeed!" O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: mṛto hy ayam ato dṛṣṭaḥ kathaṃ jīvitam āptavān kim etat tapaso vīryaṃ yenāyaṃ jīvitaḥ punaḥ śrotum icchāma viprarṣe yadi śrotavyam ity uta
english: "This one was dead, yet is seen here alive — how did he attain life again? What is this power of austerity by which he has come back to life? We wish to hear, O seer among brahmins, if it is fit to be heard."

sanskrit: sa tān uvāca nāsmākaṃ mṛtyuḥ prabhavate nṛpāḥ kāraṇaṃ vaḥ pravakṣyāmi hetuyogaṃ samāsataḥ
english: He said to them: "Death has no power over us, O kings. I shall tell you the reason — the connection of causes — briefly."

sanskrit: satyam evābhijānīmo nānṛte kurmahe manaḥ svadharmam anutiṣṭhāmas tasmān mṛtyubhayaṃ na naḥ
english: "We know only truth; we do not set our minds on falsehood; we follow our own dharma — therefore we have no fear of death."

sanskrit: yad brāhmaṇānāṃ kuśalaṃ tad eṣāṃ kathayāmahe naiṣāṃ duścaritaṃ brūmas tasmān mṛtyubhayaṃ na naḥ
english: "We speak only of what is good for brahmins; we do not speak of their misconduct — therefore we have no fear of death."

sanskrit: atithīn annapānena bhṛtyān atyaśanena ca tejasvideśavāsāc ca tasmān mṛtyubhayaṃ na naḥ
english: "We satisfy guests with food and drink, servants with abundant food, and we dwell in the abode of the splendorous — therefore we have no fear of death."

sanskrit: etad vai leśamātraṃ vaḥ samākhyātaṃ vimatsarāḥ gacchadhvaṃ sahitāḥ sarve na pāpād bhayam asti vaḥ
english: "This much only, free of envy, has been told to you. Go all together — you need have no fear on account of sin."

sanskrit: evam astv iti te sarve pratipūjya mahāmunim svadeśam agaman hṛṣṭā rājāno bharatarṣabha
english: Saying "So be it", all those kings, having honoured the great sage, went back to their own land rejoicing, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca bhūya eva tu māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ nibodha me vainyo nāmeha rājarṣir aśvamedhāya dīkṣitaḥ tam atrir gantum ārebhe vittārtham iti naḥ śrutam
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Listen further from me about the greatness of brahmins. Here a royal sage named Vainya was consecrated for the horse sacrifice; Atri undertook to go to him for the purpose of wealth — so we have heard.

sanskrit: bhūyo 'tha nānurudhyat sa dharmavyaktinidarśanāt saṃcintya sa mahātejā vanam evānvarocayat dharmapatnīṃ samāhūya putrāṃś cedam uvāca ha
english: But again he was not inclined to it on account of the clear indication of what is right; reflecting upon it, that one of great splendour chose the forest instead. Having summoned his devoted wife and his sons, he spoke thus:

sanskrit: prāpsyāmaḥ phalam atyantaṃ bahulaṃ nirupadravam araṇyagamanaṃ kṣipraṃ rocatāṃ vo guṇādhikam
english: "We shall attain an extremely abundant and untroubled fruit. Let going to the forest quickly be pleasing to you — it is superior in merit."

sanskrit: taṃ bhāryā pratyuvācedaṃ dharmam evānurudhyatī vainyaṃ gatvā mahātmānam arthayasva dhanaṃ bahu sa te dāsyati rājarṣir yajamāno 'rthine dhanam
english: His wife, devoted to dharma, replied to him thus: "Go to the great-souled Vainya and ask him for much wealth. That royal sage, the sacrificer, will give wealth to one who asks for it."

sanskrit: tata ādāya viprarṣe pratigṛhya dhanaṃ bahu bhṛtyān sutān saṃvibhajya tato vraja yathepsitam eṣa vai paramo dharmo dharmavidbhir udāhṛtaḥ
english: "Then, O seer among brahmins, having accepted and received the abundant wealth, distributing it among your dependants and sons, go thereafter as you wish. This is declared to be the highest dharma by those who know dharma."

sanskrit: atrir uvāca kathito me mahābhāge gautamena mahātmanā vainyo dharmārthasaṃyuktaḥ satyavratasamanvitaḥ
english: Atri said: "O fortunate one, the great-souled Gautama has told me about Vainya — that he is united with dharma and wealth, and endowed with the vow of truth."

sanskrit: kiṃ tv asti tatra dveṣṭāro nivasanti hi me dvijāḥ yathā me gautamaḥ prāha tato na vyavasāmy aham
english: "Yet there are those who hate me dwelling there — brahmins of mine, as Gautama has told me; therefore I am not resolved to go."

sanskrit: tatra sma vācaṃ kalyāṇīṃ dharmakāmārthasaṃhitām mayoktām anyathā brūyus tatas te vai nirarthakām
english: "They might pervert the auspicious words I spoke there, the words united with dharma, desire, and wealth — and thus render them fruitless."

sanskrit: gamiṣyāmi mahāprājñe rocate me vacas tava gāś ca me dāsyate vainyaḥ prabhūtaṃ cārthasaṃcayam
english: "I shall go, O greatly wise one — your words please me; and Vainya will give me cows and an abundant accumulation of wealth."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam uktvā jagāmāśu vainyayajñaṃ mahātapāḥ gatvā ca yajñāyatanam atris tuṣṭāva taṃ nṛpam
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having spoken thus, the great ascetic quickly went to Vainya's sacrifice. Having gone to the sacrificial ground, Atri praised that king:

sanskrit: rājan vainya tvam īśaś ca bhuvi tvaṃ prathamo nṛpaḥ stuvanti tvāṃ munigaṇās tvad anyo nāsti dharmavit
english: "O king, O Vainya, you are the lord; you are the foremost ruler upon the earth. The hosts of sages praise you; there is no one other than you who knows dharma."

sanskrit: tam abravīd ṛṣis tatra vacaḥ kruddho mahātapāḥ maivam atre punar brūyā na te prajñā samāhitā atra naḥ prathamaṃ sthātā mahendro vai prajāpatiḥ
english: Then a sage of great austerity spoke angrily to him: "Do not speak thus again, O Atri — your understanding is not collected. In this matter, our foremost authority is Mahendra, who is truly Prajāpati."

sanskrit: athātrir api rājendra gautamaṃ pratyabhāṣata ayam eva vidhātā ca yathaivendraḥ prajāpatiḥ tvam eva muhyase mohān na prajñānaṃ tavāsti ha
english: Then Atri also addressed Gautama, O lord of kings: "He is indeed the creator just as Indra is Prajāpati. It is you alone who are deluded through delusion; you have no true understanding."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca jānāmi nāhaṃ muhyāmi tvaṃ vivakṣur vimuhyase stoṣyase 'bhyudayaprepsus tasya darśanasaṃśrayāt
english: Gautama said: "I know; I am not deluded. You, wishing to speak, are deluded. You will praise him, seeking prosperity, by resorting to his presence."

sanskrit: na vettha paramaṃ dharmaṃ na cāvaiṣi prayojanam bālas tvam asi mūḍhaś ca vṛddhaḥ kenāpi hetunā
english: "You do not know the highest dharma, nor do you understand its purpose. You are childish and foolish — called an elder only by some reason or other."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca vivadantau tathā tau tu munīnāṃ darśane sthitau ye tasya yajñe saṃvṛttās te 'pṛcchanta kathaṃ tv imau
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: As those two were thus disputing in the sight of the sages, those who were assembled at his sacrifice asked: "How are these two —"

sanskrit: praveśaḥ kena datto 'yam anayor vainyasaṃsadi uccaiḥ samabhibhāṣantau kena kāryeṇa viṣṭhitau
english: "— who gave these two entry into Vainya's assembly? Speaking loudly, for what purpose do they stand here?"

sanskrit: tataḥ paramadharmātmā kāśyapaḥ sarvadharmavit vivādināv anuprāptau tāv ubhau pratyavedayat
english: Then Kaśyapa, of supremely righteous soul and versed in all dharma, presented those two disputants as they had arrived.

sanskrit: athābravīt sadasyāṃs tu gautamo munisattamān āvayor vyāhṛtaṃ praśnaṃ śṛṇuta dvijapuṃgavāḥ vainyo vidhātety āhātrir atra naḥ saṃśayo mahān
english: Then Gautama spoke to those best of sages among the assembly members: "Hear the question stated by us two, O foremost of twice-born. Atri says Vainya is the creator — herein lies our great doubt."

sanskrit: śrutvaiva tu mahātmāno munayo 'bhyadravan drutam sanatkumāraṃ dharmajñaṃ saṃśayacchedanāya vai
english: Upon hearing this, those great-souled sages quickly ran to Sanatkumāra, the knower of dharma, in order to resolve the doubt.

sanskrit: sa ca teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā yathātattvaṃ mahātapāḥ pratyuvācātha tān evaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having heard their words, that great ascetic replied to them in accordance with truth, speaking these words joined with dharma and purpose:

sanskrit: sanatkumāra uvāca brahma kṣatreṇa sahitaṃ kṣatraṃ ca brahmaṇā saha rājā vai prathamo dharmaḥ prajānāṃ patir eva ca sa eva śakraḥ śukraś ca sa dhātā sa bṛhaspatiḥ
english: Sanatkumāra said: "Brahmā joined with kshatriya power, and kshatriya power joined with brahma — the king is indeed the foremost dharma and lord of subjects. He himself is Śakra, and Śukra, and Dhata, and Bṛhaspati."

sanskrit: prajāpatir virāṭ samrāṭ kṣatriyo bhūpatir nṛpaḥ ya ebhiḥ stūyate śabdaiḥ kas taṃ nārcitum arhati
english: "Prajāpati, Virat, Samrat, kshatriya, lord of the earth, ruler — he who is praised by these titles: who would not be worthy of honouring him?"

sanskrit: purāyonir yudhājic ca abhiyā mudito bhavaḥ svarṇetā sahajid babhrur iti rājābhidhīyate
english: "Primordial source, victor in battle, fearless, joyous in being, golden-eyed, born-conqueror, tawny one — thus is the king designated."

sanskrit: satyamanyur yudhājīvaḥ satyadharmapravartakaḥ adharmād ṛṣayo bhītā balaṃ kṣatre samādadhan
english: "True in wrath, living by combat, setter of truth and dharma in motion — when the seers were afraid of adharma, they placed their strength in the kshatriya."

sanskrit: ādityo divi deveṣu tamo nudati tejasā tathaiva nṛpatir bhūmāv adharmaṃ nudate bhṛśam
english: "As the sun among the gods in heaven dispels darkness with its radiance, so too the king upon the earth mightily dispels adharma."

sanskrit: ato rājñaḥ pradhānatvaṃ śāstraprāmāṇyadarśanāt uttaraḥ sidhyate pakṣo yena rājeti bhāṣitam
english: "Therefore the king's pre-eminence is established by the authority of scripture; the latter position is proved, the one by which it is declared 'the king'."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ sa rājā saṃhṛṣṭaḥ siddhe pakṣe mahāmanāḥ tam atrim abravīt prītaḥ pūrvaṃ yenābhisaṃstutaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then that king, greatly rejoiced with his position established, that high-minded one, spoke with pleasure to Atri who had formerly praised him:

sanskrit: yasmāt sarvamanuṣyeṣu jyāyāṃsaṃ mām ihābravīḥ sarvadevaiś ca viprarṣe saṃmitaṃ śreṣṭham eva ca tasmāt te 'haṃ pradāsyāmi vividhaṃ vasu bhūri ca
english: "Since among all men here you declared me to be the greatest, O seer among brahmins, equal to all the gods and the very best — therefore I shall give you various and abundant goods."

sanskrit: dāsīsahasraṃ śyāmānāṃ suvastrāṇām alaṃkṛtam daśa koṭyo hiraṇyasya rukmabhārāṃs tathā daśa etad dadāni te vipra sarvajñas tvaṃ hi me mataḥ
english: "A thousand dark-skinned maidservants adorned with fine garments, ten crores of gold, and likewise ten loads of gold — this I give you, O brahmin; for you are in my view omniscient."

sanskrit: tad atrir nyāyataḥ sarvaṃ pratigṛhya mahāmanāḥ pratyājagāma tejasvī gṛhān eva mahātapāḥ
english: Having righteously accepted all of that, that high-minded, splendorous, great ascetic Atri returned home.

sanskrit: pradāya ca dhanaṃ prītaḥ putrebhyaḥ prayatātmavān tapaḥ samabhisaṃdhāya vanam evānvapadyata
english: Having joyfully distributed the wealth to his sons, that one of controlled soul, having resolved upon austerity, departed for the forest.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca atraiva ca sarasvatyā gītaṃ parapuraṃjaya pṛṣṭayā muninā vīra śṛṇu tārkṣyeṇa dhīmatā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: And here also, O conqueror of enemy citadels, hear what was sung by Sarasvatī when questioned by the wise sage Tarakshya, O hero.

sanskrit: tārkṣya uvāca kiṃ nu śreyaḥ puruṣasyeha bhadre; kathaṃ kurvan na cyavate svadharmāt ācakṣva me cārusarvāṅgi sarvaṃ; tvayānuśiṣṭo na cyaveyaṃ svadharmāt
english: Tarakshya said: "What indeed is highest good for a man in this world, O auspicious one? Acting how does one not fall from one's own dharma? Tell me everything, O one beautiful in all your limbs — instructed by you, may I not fall from my own dharma."

sanskrit: kathaṃ cāgniṃ juhuyāṃ pūjaye vā; kasmin kāle kena dharmo na naśyet etat sarvaṃ subhage prabravīhi; yathā lokān virajāḥ saṃcareyam
english: "How should I offer into fire, or how worship? At what time, by what means does dharma not perish? Tell me all this, O fortunate one — so that I may move through the worlds spotless."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evaṃ pṛṣṭā prītiyuktena tena; śuśrūṣum īkṣyottamabuddhiyuktam tārkṣyaṃ vipraṃ dharmayuktaṃ hitaṃ ca; sarasvatī vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Thus questioned with joy by him, beholding Tarakshya, that brahmin endowed with highest intelligence, devoted to dharma, and well-intentioned, Sarasvatī spoke these words:

sanskrit: sarasvaty uvāca yo brahma jānāti yathāpradeśaṃ; svādhyāyanityaḥ śucir apramattaḥ sa vai puro devapurasya gantā; sahāmaraiḥ prāpnuyāt prītiyogam
english: Sarasvatī said: "One who knows Brahman according to proper instruction, who is constant in self-study, pure, and vigilant — he will indeed go to the fore of the city of the gods; he will attain union with joy together with the immortals."

sanskrit: tatra sma ramyā vipulā viśokāḥ; supuṣpitāḥ puṣkariṇyaḥ supuṇyāḥ akardamā mīnavatyaḥ sutīrthā; hiraṇmayair āvṛtāḥ puṇḍarīkaiḥ
english: "There are lovely, vast, grief-free, richly blossoming sacred lotus-ponds of great merit — free of mud, full of fish, with fine bathing-ghats, surrounded by golden lotuses."

sanskrit: tāsāṃ tīreṣv āsate puṇyakarmā; mahīyamānaḥ pṛthag apsarobhiḥ supuṇyagandhābhir alaṃkṛtābhir; hiraṇyavarṇābhir atīva hṛṣṭaḥ
english: "On the banks of those ponds the doer of meritorious deeds sits, honoured separately by apsaras adorned with most holy fragrances, golden-complexioned — exceedingly joyful."

sanskrit: paraṃ lokaṃ gopradās tv āpnuvanti; dattvānaḍvāhaṃ sūryalokaṃ vrajanti vāso dattvā candramasaḥ sa lokaṃ; dattvā hiraṇyam amṛtatvam eti
english: "Givers of cows attain the highest world; those who give a bull go to the world of the sun. One who gives a garment goes to the world of the moon; one who gives gold attains immortality."

sanskrit: dhenuṃ dattvā suvratāṃ sādhudohāṃ; kalyāṇavat sāmapalāyinīṃ ca yāvanti romāṇi bhavanti tasyās; tāvad varṣāṇy aśnute svargalokam
english: "One who gives a well-behaved cow, good in milking, auspicious, gentle in nature and pace — for as many hairs as she has, for that many years does one enjoy the heavenly world."

sanskrit: anaḍvāhaṃ suvrataṃ yo dadāti; halasya voḍhāram anantavīryam dhuraṃdharaṃ balavantaṃ yuvānaṃ; prāpnoti lokān daśa dhenudasya
english: "One who gives a bull of good conduct, a bearer of the plough, of boundless vigour, yoke-bearing, powerful, and young — such a person attains ten times the worlds of the cow-giver."

sanskrit: yaḥ sapta varṣāṇi juhoti tārkṣya; havyaṃ tv agnau suvrataḥ sādhuśīlaḥ saptāvarān sapta pūrvān punāti; pitāmahān ātmanaḥ karmabhiḥ svaiḥ
english: "One who for seven years, O Tarakshya, duly offers oblations into fire, of good vow and virtuous conduct — he purifies by his own deeds seven generations forward and seven generations of his own ancestors."

sanskrit: tārkṣya uvāca kim agnihotrasya vrataṃ purāṇam; ācakṣva me pṛcchataś cārurūpe tvayānuśiṣṭo 'ham ihādya vidyāṃ; yad agnihotrasya vrataṃ purāṇam
english: Tarakshya said: "What is the ancient vow of the agnihotra? Tell me as I ask, O one of beautiful form. Instructed by you I have today the knowledge — but what is the ancient vow of the agnihotra?"

sanskrit: sarasvaty uvāca na cāśucir nāpy anirṇiktapāṇir; nābrahmavij juhuyān nāvipaścit bubhukṣavaḥ śucikāmā hi devā; nāśraddadhānād dhi havir juṣanti
english: Sarasvatī said: "One who is impure, or one whose hands are unwashed, one ignorant of Brahman, or one without discernment — should not offer; for the gods desire purity and do not accept oblations from one who lacks faith."

sanskrit: nāśrotriyaṃ devahavye niyuñjyān; moghaṃ parā siñcati tādṛśo hi apūrṇam aśrotriyam āha tārkṣya; na vai tādṛg juhuyād agnihotram
english: "One should not engage one ignorant of the Vedas in the gods' oblation — such a one pours fruitlessly into the beyond; the one ignorant of the Vedas is declared incomplete, O Tarakshya; such a one should not offer the agnihotra."

sanskrit: kṛśānuṃ ye juhvati śraddadhānāḥ; satyavratā hutaśiṣṭāśinaś ca gavāṃ lokaṃ prāpya te puṇyagandhaṃ; paśyanti devaṃ paramaṃ cāpi satyam
english: "Those who offer to fire with faith, who hold the vow of truth and eat the remnants of oblations — having attained the world of cows with its holy fragrance, they behold the Supreme God and Truth itself."

sanskrit: tārkṣya uvāca kṣetrajñabhūtāṃ paralokabhāve; karmodaye buddhim atipraviṣṭām prajñāṃ ca devīṃ subhage vimṛśya; pṛcchāmi tvāṃ kā hy asi cārurūpe
english: Tarakshya said: "Reflecting upon you — one who has become a knower of the field in the nature of the other world, whose intelligence has deeply entered into the arising of karma, and who bears a divine wisdom, O fortunate one — I ask you: who indeed are you, O one of beautiful form?"

sanskrit: sarasvaty uvāca agnihotrād aham abhyāgatāsmi; viprarṣabhāṇāṃ saṃśayacchedanāya tvatsaṃyogād aham etad abruvaṃ; bhāve sthitā tathyam arthaṃ yathāvat
english: Sarasvatī said: "I have come forth from the agnihotra, to resolve the doubt of the foremost among brahmin seers. Through my meeting with you I have spoken all this — standing in truth, the true meaning exactly as it is."

sanskrit: tārkṣya uvāca na hi tvayā sadṛśī kā cid asti; vibhrājase hy atimātraṃ yathā śrīḥ rūpaṃ ca te divyam atyantakāntaṃ; prajñāṃ ca devīṃ subhage bibharṣi
english: Tarakshya said: "There is indeed no one equal to you; you shine exceedingly like Śrī herself. Your form is divine and supremely lovely, and you bear a divine wisdom, O fortunate one."

sanskrit: sarasvaty uvāca śreṣṭhāni yāni dvipadāṃ variṣṭha; yajñeṣu vidvann upapādayanti tair evāhaṃ saṃpravṛddhā bhavāmi; āpyāyitā rūpavatī ca vipra
english: Sarasvatī said: "The finest things which the best of two-footed beings, O learned one, offer at sacrifices — by those very things I grow and flourish; nourished by them I become beautiful in form, O brahmin."
